stem.text: The number of fish P in a lake is modeled by the differential equation \( \frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{P}{3} - \frac{P^{2}}{5100} \), where t is measured in months, and \( P(0) = 340 \). Without solving the equation, find the limit of P as t increases without bound, and the value of P at which P is growing fastest.

answer_key.label: P approaches \( 1700 \) fish as t increases without bound, and P is growing fastest when \( P = 850 \) fish.

worked_solution.text: The right side equals \( \frac{1}{3}P\left(1 - \frac{P}{1700}\right) \), which is 0 at P = 0 and at P = 1700, so the carrying capacity is 1700.
worked_solution.rule_named: zeros of the logistic right side

worked_solution.text: For 0 < P < 1700 the right side is positive, and P(0) = 340 lies in that range, so P increases and approaches 1700 fish as t increases without bound.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the rate gives the limit

worked_solution.text: The right side is a quadratic in P that opens downward with zeros at 0 and 1700, so it is largest halfway between them, at P = 850 fish; P passes through that value because it starts below it.

options.label: P approaches \( 0 \) fish as t increases without bound, and P is growing fastest when \( P = 850 \) fish.
options.derivation: the limiting value read from the other zero of the right side, P = 0

options.label: P approaches \( 340 \) fish as t increases without bound, and P is growing fastest when \( P = 850 \) fish.
options.derivation: a limit named without using the sign of the rate, the initial value taken as the level the population settles at

options.label: P approaches \( 1700 \) fish as t increases without bound, and P is growing fastest when \( P = 1700 \) fish.
options.derivation: the value of fastest growth reported as the carrying capacity itself
